test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Machinist) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In taper turning by the tailstock offset method, a job has a large diameter (D) of 60 mm, a small diameter (d) of 40 mm, a taper length (l) of 200 mm and a total job length (L) of 800 mm. What will be the required tailstock offset?
solution:
The correct answer is __40 mm.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The formula for tailstock offset in taper turning is (D - d) × L / (2 × l)__.
 
• Substituting the values: (60 - 40) × 800 / (2 × 200).
 
• This simplifies to __20 × 800 / 400 = 40 mm__.
 
• Hence, the required tailstock offset is __40 mm.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Taper Turning:**

 
 
• It is a machining process used to produce a conical shape on a cylindrical job.
 
• Methods include tailstock offset, form tool, and compound rest techniques.
 
 
 
• **Tailstock Offset Method:**
 
 
• Involves shifting the tailstock laterally to create a taper.
 
• Used for gradual and accurate taper machining.
